observation.visible_scene: A steep, snow- and rock-dusted mountainside occupies the lower-left corner, while the rest of the frame is filled with dense, billowing white-gray cloud or fog. The right side of the cloud mass is brightly sunlit, the left and center are darker and shadowed. A thin, near-vertical bright streak (consistent in horizontal position throughout) is faintly visible through the mist near the center-bottom, suggesting a fixed feature such as a waterfall or jet rather than moving vapor.
visible_changes: The cloud/fog continuously churns and deforms: its internal texture, edges, and the boundary between the dark left mass and the bright right mass shift from frame to frame.
The bright sunlit cloud on the right gradually encroaches toward the center over the excerpt, while the dark shadowed region on the left reshapes and drifts.
The snow-dusted ridge at lower-left stays in roughly the same screen position, sometimes more or less obscured by passing cloud, indicating the slope is a stationary backdrop.
The thin vertical streak remains at a fixed horizontal location across all frames, intermittently clearer or hazier as cloud moves in front of it.
Overall framing of the ridge is stable, so the dominant motion is the cloud's own rolling/translation rather than a large camera move.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause or source of the cloud/fog and of the vertical streak is not shown.
What lies beyond the right and top edges, and the state of the scene before t=0 or after t=3.2s, is unknown.
uncertain_details: Whether the bright vertical streak is a waterfall, a jet, or a fixed structural feature cannot be confirmed.
Any slight camera drift versus pure cloud motion is hard to separate because the only static reference is the small visible ridge.
Distinguishing cloud translation from cloud deformation is approximate; both appear to occur.
